content: ## Metadata_Start ## code: en ## title: Advanced Embedding ## slug: iframes-advanced-embedding ## seoTitle: Advanced Embedding ## description: ## contentType: Markdown ## Metadata_End The first step in the embedding process is to allowlist any domains you plan on using. ## Allowlisting Domains {{snippet.Iframes_AllowlistingDomains}} ## Add a Demo Domain {{snippet.Iframes_AddDemoDomain}} ## Set Up an Advanced Embedded Site If you want to control every aspect of the {{variable.Object_Event}}'s iframe, we recommend using the [Advanced Embedding tool](https://demo.events.blackthorn.io/blackthorn/advanced.html){target=`_blank`}. This tool provides the option to use Events Listeners. Event Admins can use them to control the iframe's behavior and perform actions when the {{variable.Object_Event}}s are triggered. ### The Basics For this example, we will use an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} with the {{variable.Field_ETGroup_EventGroupURL}} set to “https://events.blackthorn.io/en/3itLbC6/g/ZZ8AC6qtdC”. The first thing the Event Admin needs to do is initialize the BT Events `embed.js`. You do this by pasting the following script on the parent website where the {{variable.Object_Event}} will be embedded: ``` ``` Now, you need to get the `orgId` and `path` parameters from the {{variable.Object_Event}}/{{variable.Object_EventGroup}} webpage that will be embedded. The `orgId` will be the same for all {{variable.Object_Event}}s in your org. It is the first parameter immediately after the language parameter. In this example, the `orgId` parameter is “3itLbC6”. ![Iframe_Advanced Embedding_orgId](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Iframe_Advanced%20Embedding_orgId.png){height="" width=""} Now, you need to extract the `path`, which is the remainder of the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventPageURL}} or {{variable.Field_ETGroup_EventGroupURL}}. In this example, the path is “/g/ZZ8AC6qtdC”. Next, you need to create an HTML container that will contain the iframe. It will look something like this: ```html ``` The container is currently empty, but you will insert the iframe later. To embed the {{variable.Object_Event}} or {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} webpage, create the following: ```html // The minimal code to create an embed events in your page var app = new EventsApp({ orgId: '3itLbC6', path: '/g/ZZ8AC6qtdC', }); app.mount('.events-container'); ``` Notice that the app.mount targets the .events-container class. This lets the parent container know where the iframe will live on the parent page. The whole snippet will look like this. There are also some basic styling parameters, such as height, min-height, and width, that you can update as needed. ```html var app = new EventsApp({ orgId: "3itLbC6", path: "g/ZZ8AC6qtdC", height: "100%", width: "100%", }); // This indicates where the iFrame will be mounted app.mount('.events-container'); ``` #### Example 1 [Event Group embedded on a sample website](https://carlosdmendoza.github.io/Redirect-Demo/advance-embedding-2.html){target=`_blank`} @(Embed)(https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Advanced%20Embedding_Event%20Group.mp4){height="320" width="640"} #### Example 2 [Event Group embedded on a website with a footer and header](https://carlosdmendoza.github.io/Redirect-Demo/advance-embedding.html){target=`_blank`} @(Embed)(https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Advanced%20Embedding_Event%20Group%20with%20header%20and%20footer.mp4){height="320" width="640"} ## Event Listeners ### CONTENT_SIZE_CHANGED Placing an iframe in a parent website creates two scrollbars - one for the iframe and one for the parent website. To remove one of the scrollbars and improve the user experience, use the CONTENT_SIZE_CHANGED Event Listener that the Events iframe offers. It will set a custom height based on the size of the content. Using the following iframe structure, this is how it works. ```html var app = new EventsApp({ orgId: "3itLbC6", path: "g/ZZ8AC6qtdC", height: "100%", width: "100%", }); app.mount('.events-container'); ``` Add `scrolling: “no”,` as a parameter to remove the iframe scrollbar. Add the Event Listener code. ``` listeners: [ { event: "CONTENT_SIZE_CHANGED", handler: function (params) { // We are targeting here the events-container (Where the iframe is) const container = document.querySelector(".events-container"); if (container) { // Apply the dynamic height container.style.height = params.height + "px"; } // This is the parent container where the events-container is. const content = document.querySelector(".content"); if (content) { content.style.minHeight = params.height + "px"; content.style.height = params.height + "px"; } }, }, ] ``` The new code will appear as follows: ```html var app = new EventsApp({ orgId: "5e53zvb7", path: "g/7BBXYj8cW9", height: "100%", width: "100%", scrolling: "no", listeners: [ { event: "CONTENT_SIZE_CHANGED", handler: function (params) { // We are targeting here the events-container (Where the iframe is) const container = document.querySelector(".events-container"); if (container) { // Apply the dynamic height container.style.height = params.height + "px"; } // This is the parent container where the events-container is. const content = document.querySelector(".content"); if (content) { content.style.minHeight = params.height + "px"; content.style.height = params.height + "px"; } }, }, ], }); // This indicates where the iFrame will be mounted app.mount('.events-container'); ``` **Example:** Here’s a [sample of the website](https://carlosdmendoza.github.io/Redirect-Demo/dynamic-sizing.html){target=`_blank`} with the updates. @(Embed)(https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Dynamic%20Sizing%20and%20No%20Scroll%20bar%20for%20iFrames.mp4){height="320" width="640"} ### ROUTE_CHANGED Another common issue with iframes is how they scroll when opening a new page. For example, if the iframe is smaller than the page you are scrolling, the iframe doesn’t always scroll up automatically when an {{variable.Object_Event}} is opened from an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. @(Embed)(https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/iFrames%20wont%20scroll%20to%20top%20automatically.mp4){height="320" width="640"} Use the ROUTE_CHANGED Event Listener to prevent this from happening whenever the iframe changes routes. This code instructs the iframe to start from the top of the screen instead of remaining in the previously scrolled position. ``` “{ event: 'ROUTE_CHANGED', handler: function(params) { routeChangeCount++; // The reason for this is so that the page doesn't scroll to the iFrame on page load. // (There are two route changes before the iFrame actually loads) if (routeChangeCount let routeChangeCount = 0; // Counter for route changes /* We are defining org id whoch is the first parameter of event group url The reason for height and width parameters is to ensure the iFrame take all the available space on the parent container. That is later updated by a variable as page changes. */ var app = new EventsApp({ orgId: '5e53zvb7', path: "g/7BBXYj8cW9?date=ALL,ALL", height: "100%", width: "100%", listeners: [ { event: 'ROUTE_CHANGED', handler: function(params) { routeChangeCount++; // The reason for this is so that the page doesn't scroll to the iFrame on page load. // (There are two route changes before the iFrame actually loads) if (routeChangeCount ``` To review, we have made the following changes to the code above. * We added a count to the ROUTE_CHANGED Event Listener, so the scrollbar only scrolls to the top after the second ROUTE_CHANGED. This is because a redirect occurs as soon as the page loads. If we don’t add the count, the user’s focus will be on the iframe when the page loads, which we don’t want. * The added “window.scrollTo” instructs the browser to focus on the container with the class name “.content” which is the parent container where the iframe was inserted. This occurs while maintaining the code for content-resizing (see above). You can see the new behavior on this [sample website](https://carlosdmendoza.github.io/Redirect-Demo/scroll-to-top.html){target=`_blank`} with the embedded iframe. @(Embed)(https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Scroll%20to%20Top%20automatically.mp4){height="320" width="640"} Notice how the iframe integrates better with the parent website. There is a smooth transition to the top of the page, so the reader’s eye always remains focused on important content on the parent page. ### FORM_SUBMITTED The FORM_SUBMITTED Event Listener has many use cases, ranging from redirecting users to a new page after completing the registration process or extracting data from the registration form directly to the parent website. (Post-registration Form answers will not trigger the Event Listener.) When an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} submits a {{variable.Object_Form}}, the host page receives a FORM_SUBMITTED event with the following details from the pre-registration {{variable.Object_Form}}. * `path` - form submission URL path * `name` - form name * `data` - form submission data Event Admins can set up and use the listener as needed. Here’s a demo of how it can be used. #### Tracking Form Responses with Google Your organization’s Google Analytics account can "listen" to {{variable.Object_Event}}s in an iframe to link the Attendee journey to your main Google Analytics account with an Event Listener. The Google Analytics ID entered in the Salesforce org will determine which Google Analytics account the collected data will go to. In this example, the Google Analytics account will use the FORM_SUBMITTED Event Listener to complete the following steps. 1. “Listen” to Form changes 2. Extract the changes from the iframe 3. Collect the data for the Google Analytics account 4. Redirect the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} to a new page after completing the checkout process In this example, you will see this code. ```javascript { event: “FORM_SUBMITTED”, handler: function (params). { logEvent(“FORM_SUBMITTED: “ + JSON.stringify(params)}; onFormSubmitted(): // Call the function to handle the submission }, }, ``` and ```javascript // Function to handle the form submitted event function onFormSubmitted( ) { // Open Google.com in a new tab when the event is triggered window.open(“https://www.google.com”, “_blank”); } ``` While an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} registers for an {{variable.Object_Event}}, the Event Listener listens and then opens a separate page, www.google.com, in a new blank tab outside the iframe. This process can also be performed using the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventPageURL}} or the website of your choice. 1. Complete the Event registration process, but don’t click the **Register** button. 2. Before clicking **Register**, look at the code to see that no {{variable.Object_Form}}s have been submitted. 3. Click **Register**. 4. You will be redirected to the URL that was added to the code. In this case, a blank Google.com tab opens. 5. The ERS records are processed in the background. 6. The resulting code shows the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} form data (first name, last name, email, language, question answers, and the `path` (where the form was submitted)). @(Embed)(https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Demo%20URL%20redirect%20using%20the%20FORM_SUBMITTED.mp4){height="320" width="640"} ### APP_READY The APP_READY Event Listener notifies the parent page when the iframe is done loading and emits a boolean value that the Event Admin can use to perform tasks. Those tasks may include showing a custom preloader on the whole website while the iframe is loaded or a message instructing the user that something is loading. By default, Blackthorn shows a loader screen, but if you want to customize the user experience, the APP_READY Event Listener is available. ## Embed a Media Player {{variable.Feature_Iframe}} injectors allow Admins to embed iframes on a {{variable.Object_CustomContent}} record. This feature is behind a feature flag, which means it can be enabled on a per org basis on the License record (LMO). To enable it, add a License Metadata entry for CONTENT_IFRAME_ENABLED with the value true. To add an iframe to a {{variable.Object_CustomContent}} record, enter iframe data, like the following example, in the {{variable.Field_CustomContent_Content}} rich text field. "[embed prop1="xxx" prop2="xxx" .... propn="xxx"] [/embed]" where props are the required properties for the iframe (width, height, src, ….). ![embed media player](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/embed%20media%20player.png){height="" width=""} If the feature is not enabled via License Metadata, the embed tag will be shown as plain text.
